title: The step-by-step process collection
subtitle: Trace reactions, host–pathogen processes, and drug journeys through interactive sequences.

blocks.title: One reaction, alternative products
blocks.description: The process identity stays fixed. The result control changes only the product produced by this reaction.

steps.title: Substrate
steps.description: Define the substrate and reaction conditions.

steps.title: Enzyme–substrate complex
steps.description: Describe binding and catalytic commitment.

steps.title: Product A
steps.description: Default product of this one reaction.

steps.title: Product B
steps.description: Alternative result of the same reaction under the stated conditions.

blocks.title: One pathogenic process, alternative results
blocks.description: The same host–pathogen process may resolve or progress; the control changes the result, not the pathway.

steps.title: Exposure
steps.description: Specify the pathogen and entry route.

steps.title: Establishment
steps.description: Explain establishment in the host.

steps.title: Host–pathogen interaction
steps.description: Define the shared process that can produce different results.

steps.title: Persistent tissue injury
steps.description: Default result when injury-producing mechanisms persist.

steps.title: Clearance and resolution
steps.description: Alternative result of the same host–pathogen process.

blocks.title: One drug mechanism, alternative results
blocks.description: The drug and target pathway remain fixed; the control changes only the resulting effect.

steps.title: Drug exposure
steps.description: Specify the drug and clinically relevant exposure context.

steps.title: Target engagement
steps.description: Specify one receptor, enzyme, transporter, or channel.

steps.title: Therapeutic result
steps.description: Default result produced through this drug–target mechanism.

steps.title: Adverse result
steps.description: Alternative result produced through the same drug–target mechanism.

blocks.title: Track one pathway over time
blocks.description: The left rail records when each stage occurs. The process identity remains fixed; the result control changes only the possible result.

steps.title: Initial stage
steps.description: Define the initial state and starting time.

steps.title: Intermediate stage
steps.description: Explain what occurs at this time point.

steps.title: Result A
steps.description: Default result of this same pathway.

steps.title: Result B
steps.description: Alternative result of the same pathway at this time point.

blocks.title: Track one pathway across locations
blocks.description: The left rail records the anatomical or cellular location of each stage.

steps.title: Stage in the liver
steps.description: Explain the event occurring in this location.

steps.title: Stage in circulation
steps.description: Explain the event occurring during circulation.

steps.title: Stage at the target organ
steps.description: Explain the event occurring at the target location.

blocks.title: Skin from surface to subcutis
blocks.description: Select a slab to peel through the tissue in anatomical order. Separate the stack when you need to compare boundaries and relative thickness.

layers.title: Epidermis
layers.description: Avascular epithelial barrier renewed by keratinocytes moving toward the surface.
layers.clinicalNote: The thickness and named strata vary by body site.

layers.title: Papillary dermis
layers.description: A superficial connective-tissue zone that interdigitates with the epidermis.
layers.boundaryAfter: Transition to dense irregular connective tissue

layers.title: Reticular dermis
layers.description: The thicker load-bearing dermal layer containing coarse collagen bundles and skin appendages.
layers.clinicalNote: Incisions and burns are described partly by how deeply they cross this layer.

layers.title: Subcutaneous tissue
layers.description: A mobile deep compartment connecting skin to the underlying fascia.

blocks.title: Trace an oral compound through the body
blocks.description: The tracer separates location, physical or chemical form, timing, transfer, and conceptual availability. Percentages are illustrative authoring data, not measured pharmacokinetics.

stages.title: Dose enters the gastrointestinal tract
stages.description: Define disintegration, dissolution, and the factors that make the compound available for absorption.

stages.title: Compound crosses the intestinal barrier
stages.description: State the dominant transport route and any luminal or epithelial loss.

stages.title: Presystemic handling changes exposure
stages.description: Represent extraction, biotransformation, activation, or inactivation without implying a fixed value.

stages.title: Circulation distributes the compound
stages.description: Connect perfusion, binding, and membrane permeability to tissue exposure.

stages.title: Target engagement produces a response
stages.description: Distinguish target-site exposure from the downstream physiological effect.

details.label: Teaching question
details.value: Is the response limited by delivery, binding, signaling, or adaptation?

stages.title: Parent compound or metabolites leave the body
stages.description: Describe filtration, secretion, reabsorption, and the meaning of residual body burden.
